summary: This Wikipedia-derived note surveys Southampton, a major south coast English port city in Hampshire. It covers the city's economy and employers, local media, fire cover, the University of Southampton, its charter-based governance history, Southampton Airport, its spa and seabathing history, its links to Cunard ships, the medieval friars' water supply, leisure facilities, parliamentary representation, and basic geography and demographics.
one_line: Overview of Southampton, a major south coast English port city in Hampshire, covering its economy, university, history, transport and governance.
key_facts: Ordnance Survey, the UK's national mapping agency, opened a new headquarters on the outskirts of Southampton in February 2011.
Ford's Southampton Assembly Plant in Swaythling manufactures the majority of Ford's Transit models; its closure was announced in 2012 for 2013, with the loss of hundreds of jobs.
The University of Southampton was founded in 1862 and received its Royal Charter as a university in 1952, and has over 22,000 students.
In the 2010 THES - QS World University Rankings the University of Southampton was positioned in the top 80 universities in the world.
Southampton became a spa town in 1740, and was a popular site for sea bathing by the 1760s.
The Cunard liner RMS Queen Elizabeth 2 departed Southampton for the final time on 11 November 2008.
Constructed in 1290, the friars' water supply system carried water some 1.7 kilometres from Conduit Head to the friary inside the town walls.
The charter dated 27 June 1640 gave the formal title 'The Town and County of the Town of Southampton'.
On 24 February 1964 a Charter of Elizabeth II created the City and County of the City of Southampton.
Southampton Airport is a regional airport located in the town of Eastleigh, just north of the city.
Southampton lies 75 miles (121 km) south-west of London and 19 miles (31 km) north-west of Portsmouth.
The city has an estimated population of 253,651 and is a unitary authority.
In January 2007 the average annual salary in Southampton was £22,267, £1,700 lower than the national average.

Southampton has three parliamentary members: Royston Smith (Conservative) for Southampton Itchen, Dr. Alan Whitehead (Labour) for Southampton Test, and Caroline Nokes (Conservative) for Romsey and Southampton North.
